must_fix.issue: Repeated end-of-section boilerplate. A version of 'Your Wedded Advisor confirms ... in writing' closes all seven regions (Cyclades, Crete, Dodecanese, Corfu, Athens, Peloponnese, Halkidiki), and a long 'Not published' line ends almost every venue. Readers called it a template and a sales loop.
must_fix.fix: Keep the Advisor line in two places only: under the comparison table and in the closing section (which already says it best: 'A Wedded Advisor asks each venue on your shortlist and puts the answers in writing.'). Delete the closers at the end of the Crete, Dodecanese, Corfu, Athens, Peloponnese and Halkidiki sections, and cut the Cyclades closer to the venue facts (see the packages note under consider). Let each region end on its last venue fact. Keep every 'Not published' line (they build trust with the primary reader and the sceptic), but trim each to the two or three items that matter most for that venue, leading with exclusive use and curfew where they apply. Add no new facts.

should_fix.issue: No accessibility information. Grace Hotel's split-level terrace and the Santorini clifftop venues raise questions about steps for older guests. Kokotos Estate is the only venue that mentions access, and it has no bedrooms. The primary couple's grandparents worry (cross-island transfers, ferry luggage) is the same concern.
should_fix.fix: Make no access claims about any venue beyond what the draft already sources. In 'How to compare Greece wedding venues like for like', add one line in a confident voice: 'If an older guest or anyone with limited mobility is coming, ask each venue for the route from guest rooms to the ceremony and reception: steps, lifts and level paths.' Add 'step-free access' to the list of house rules the Wedded Advisor confirms in writing in the closing section. Do not add an accessibility column to the table and do not label any venue as hard going.

should_fix.issue: The page is hard to use on a phone or iPad: there is a long scroll through the overview and how-to-compare sections before the first region, and the six-column, 20-row table needs sideways swiping.
should_fix.fix: After Key takeaways, add a short jump list that links to each of the seven region headings, then Getting there, When to marry, Legal and the FAQ. Keep the table and its columns, since the primary couple and the sceptic value it. Note for cms-publisher: the table must scroll horizontally on mobile.

should_fix.issue: The page reads as Australians only. 'Quotes in AUD and works in your time zone' made a Singapore reader and an international family wonder whether the service is for them.
should_fix.fix: Keep AUD, because the brief's reader is Australian. Use the brand-facts wording 'quotes in AUD for Australian couples' in the table CTA and in the closing section, and add the brand-facts line that Wedded Concierge 'plans venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world'. Make no other claims about the service.

consider.issue: Package framing comes too early: 'ready-made options' in the intro and 'start from a set itinerary ... destination wedding packages' in the Cyclades closer made a high-value reader feel like a standard package client.
consider.fix: Change the intro to 'For our hand-picked venues, see our curated Greece wedding collection' and drop 'ready-made options'. Move the packages link out of the Cyclades section into the final paragraph of the closing section, next to the collection and magazine links.

consider.issue: The travel section leans on public transport (express buses, metro, ferry luggage) and says nothing about private arrivals or transfers.
consider.fix: Keep the ferry and EES lines (see conflicts). Add one line framed as a question to ask, with no new facts: 'For older guests or a wedding party that prefers not to take the ferry, ask each venue what private transfers it can arrange from Athens or the nearest island airport.'

consider.issue: The legal section gives a checklist for the municipality but nothing on the venue contract: which language, which currency, and how the deposit is held.
consider.fix: Add one general question to the closing section or the comparison section, with no claims about Wedded Wonderland's own terms (deposit and contract terms are deferred business details): 'Before you pay a deposit, ask which language and currency the venue contract is in and how the deposit is held.'

consider.issue: The sceptic asks whose prices the AUD quotes are and whether there is a mark-up.
consider.fix: In the closing section you may add the brand-facts line: 'Suppliers are paid at standardised industry rates, so you are never quoted a marked-up price.' Do not mention commissions, how the fee is calculated or whether the first call is free; these are deferred.

consider.issue: The primary couple (60 to 90 guests, half flying in) want a pointer to which venues fit their size.
consider.fix: Optionally extend the FAQ 'Which Greek island is best for a wedding with 100 guests?' so it names, from figures already in the draft, the venues whose published capacity and rooms on site fit 60 to 100. Add no new figures.

consider.issue: The donkey ride at Melenos Lindos reads as off-tone to a high-value reader.
consider.fix: Leave it as is. It is a sourced, distinctive detail for that venue, and the brief's reader is not the UHNW persona.

keep: Intro numbers: 'A caldera terrace in Oia suits 40 people. A Riviera resort half an hour from central Athens hosts up to 1,000.' (search_visitor, sceptic, uhnw, planner_couple)

conflicts_resolved: Ferry and public-transport detail: uhnw found it backpacker-ish, while funding_parent and planner_couple (primary) called the ferry line honest and decisive. Keep it for the primary reader, and add only a general question about private transfers.

'Not published' lines: search_visitor and uhnw found them repetitive, while planner_couple (primary) and sceptic said the honest blanks are why they trust the numbers. Keep every line and trim each to the items that matter.

AUD and Australian framing: search_visitor and uhnw felt excluded, but the brief's reader is an Australian couple. Keep AUD, scope it as 'for Australian couples' and add the brand-facts 'anywhere in the world' line.
Price ballpark: search_visitor wants one, but the house rule is no prices without Nic's sign-off. Print no figure.
Legal checklist: uhnw would delegate it, while planner_couple and funding_parent value it. Keep it.

Business details (who is on the ground on the day, a named contact or first call, commissions, the fee model, deposits held by Wedded Wonderland, a real wedding to link, security and privacy) are deferred by instruction. They are not must-fix and go to open_questions.
